newsitem.title: INDIA: Legal web closes in on India's Rao.
newsitem.headline: Legal web closes in on India's Rao.

text.p: Pressure mounted on former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao to relinquish his last major political post on Thursday as he appeared for the second time before a trial judge in a criminal case.
Rao sat silently through the second and last day of a bail hearing in a seven-year-old case of criminal forgery.
His lawyer, R.K. Anand, repeated a request for the extension of bail protecting Rao against arrest. Temporary bail, which was granted on October 9, expires next Wednesday.

Before adjourning the hearing, chief metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar told the court, packed with journalists and members of Rao's Congress party, that he would rule on the bail request next Tuesday.

If denied bail next week, Rao could be arrested and taken into custody pending completion of the trial. Anand argued that Rao's need for round-the-clock security guards would pose a problem if he were taken into police custody in a jail.
On Wednesday, federal police indicted Rao in a vote-buying case, hours after he had made his first appearance in the special court room in the forgery case.
The indictment piled pressure on Rao to step down as head of the Congress party's parliamentary delegation, newspapers said.

Rao, who resigned as prime minister in May after Congress was defeated in a general election, quit as Congress party leader in September after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court in a third criminal case, involving alleged cheating.

But he has remained head of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) and retains influence over India's 13-party United Front (UF) coalition, which depends on Congress's backing to survive a challenge from right-wing Hindu nationalists.

The Asian Age said Rao was likely to step down as CPP leader. Referring to the indictment in the 1993 vote-buying case, the newspaper said "it was unlikely that he would retain the post now that he was charge-sheeted in a fresh case".
The Observer said the fresh indictment had "come as a shot in the arm for the Rao-detractors within the party, while giving anxious moments to the United Front coalition government".
The newspaper said Rao's woes "may precipitate a review of the Congress-UF relationship in the backdrop of the persistent demand perpetuated by Rao opponents".
If Rao stepped down as CPP leader, pressure could mount on Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda to include Congress members in his cabinet, the Observer said.
But such a move would be contested by left-wing parties in the government coalition that have strained ties with Congress.

On Wednesday, Rao became the first former or serving prime minister to appear in court on criminal charges. Rao and five others have been charged with trying to defame a rival politician in 1989 by using forged bank documents.

Rao has also been named, but not charged, in a 13-year-old case of criminal conspiracy to cheat. A judge has scheduled a trial hearing for next Wednesday. Rao has not been granted pre-emptive bail in that case.
